tldr: Page 58 contains public comment submissions from diverse Oregon stakeholders on economic competitiveness. Commenters emphasize: clean energy job creation with labor standards; reducing business regulatory burden, permitting delays, and tax complexity (especially CAT); improving workforce alignment and training; addressing energy grid capacity constraints; and supporting regional economic development. Common themes include criticism of Oregon's business climate perception, need for predictable regulatory timelines, and infrastructure gaps limiting business location.

bullets.text: Oregon's clean energy sector sustained 67,000 in-state jobs in 2023; E2's 2025 Clean Jobs America report identifies 57,860 clean energy workers with 11.2% growth since 2020
Graham Trainor advocates prevailing wage law expansion would create 5,400 jobs, boost economy by $752 million, and generate $35 million in public investment
Dave Dillon reports Oregon business tax burden rose by 1/3 from 2019-2023 (increase of $3.4 billion); 28% of jobs paid under $20/hour, 57% under $30/hour in 2023
Nora Apter cites Oregon Energy Strategy modeling projecting up to 16,500 jobs by 2035; notes 2023 drought/heat caused $14.8 billion damages and 247 deaths
Sara Odendahl recommends business climate package with predictable permitting timelines, integrated workforce system, and coordinated economic development tools across agencies
Marcus Kauffman proposes dedicated Mass Timber Strategist position at Business Oregon, sector-specific workforce curricula, and predictable permitting pathways for mass timber industry
Holly Junge requests rescission of Climate Protection Program Executive Order, citing potential compliance costs exceeding $1 million/year for HP; advocates geothermal and nuclear power alternatives
Jessie Kochaver calls for transmission authority model based on Washington SB 6355, Colorado CETA, and New Mexico RETA to address grid expansion as core economic infrastructure
Multiple commenters identify permitting delays, regulatory uncertainty, grid capacity constraints, and workforce skill gaps as top barriers to business investment and clean energy deployment
Executive Order 25-29 directs ODOE and state agencies to address electricity supply, transmission siting, and clean energy project barriers with implementation deadlines September-November 2026
